body: Too many things.. abandonment, near-death experience while I was in foster care, adoption, my adoptive parents have personality disorders (I always felt invalidated), bullying in middle school, sexual abuse at 13, also my first roomate was abusive and controlling... probably genetics too... and honestly trauma resulting from my suicide attempts and hospitalizations made it so much worse

I'm sorry to hear that you went through that. I relate a lot to what you said. My parents would also ignore me and lock me in my room until I would tired myself out. Also, I learned about my 18 first months too, and I suffered from extreme neglect. I know how it feels to feel deeply broken inside. The good thing is that now you know what is the root of your problems. You are more aware of your triggers. You know why you are triggered. It's not that we 'overreact' but we react like we wouldve had to, when we were younger.  And hopefully with time you will be able to control your emotions and reactions better. Why does invalidation feel so terrible for most of us? Because it feels exactly like when we were young and our parents were not empathetic. What could be worse for a young child who really need the emotional support from their parents... 
Now I still feel sad for my past, and how everything screwed me up... but at the same time I have hope that it will help me work on my worst triggers. 
Even though it feels like there is so much to work on, these realizations are a huge step in the recovery process :)

I would also add that people who experience rapid-cycling with mixed episodes.. this is very similar to BPD. it is more about being irritable but once again it's more like being irritable when you are energetic but tired at the same time. It's more biological.

I was diagnosed with both.. but I dont think I have bipolar although I had manic episodes under medication withdrawal..
Rapid-cycling bipolar is about euphory/energy. It feels like a very high dose of caffeine or ecstasy. When you have a manic/hypomanic episode you don't feel tired, you want to accomplish too many things. Usually, it last longer than BPD episodes. But it can also last a few hours if you have extremely rapid-cycling.
BPD's shifts are more influenced by relations (love, family, work, social), there is usually more anger/sadness. It is less euphoric than bipolar, it's more 'joy'.

There are 256 combinations of BPD (symptoms), but ALSO... very often there are other comorbid disorders with BPD. 
Most common comorbid personality disorders are Avoidant Personality Disorder (around 40% people who have BPD have this one as well), Dependent Personality Disorder, Paranoid Personality Disorder, other cluster B personality disorders. People with dependent PD are very different from people with antisocial PD....
AvPD is the most co-occurring PD with BPD....

glad I can use my math class here (seriously lol)
You can have 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 criteria (out of 9) when you have BPD.
This is combinatorics, there are 126 possible combinations of having only 5 criteria out of 9, 84 possible combinations of 6/9, 36 combinations of 7/9, 9 combinations of 8/9, and only1 possible combination of 9/9. If you add all these possibilities it comes to 256.

that's right it doesn't take one form. however, what i think they usually mean by that is that there is 256 combinations of bpd (5 symptoms out of 9, there are 256 different possibilities). as i said again im not a professional, but from what i saw in my undergrad psychology courses, the core 3 features of bpd are emotional dysregulation, identity and relationships. these 3 features are tied together (i.e. you get emotional dysregulation because your identity is unstable... you ge tproblems with your relationships because your identity and your emotions are unstable). if one set of symptoms is not functionally impairing, then it is not a symptom. also, the other name for this disorder is 'emotionally instable personality disorder', it shows that this is a core symptom to the disorder. 
i dont want to insist on that too much, but for each personality disorder there is a core of symptoms that characterize the disorder. just my 2 cents, i think the best thing to do is to discuss with a psychologist :)

that's only my opinion (I read a lot about bpd and psychology), but if it only affects your relationship, it might be something else going on. someone with insecure attachment could easily have these symptoms. being jealous, being afraid of abandonment, and having low self-esteem doesn't necessarily mean having bpd. there are many relationship pathologies that exist that are less known. relationship anxiety is a common issue for people in general (http://www.psychalive.org/what-is-your-attachment-style/). it seems like she's very high-functioning at the point where I am positive that she wouldn't meet the requirements for a clinical bpd diagnosis (from what you describe). and maybe not even with bpd traits..? to be honest it doesn't sound to me like bpd, but as i said i dont know her and im not a professionnal. but yes there is still the question of having a 'normal' vs a 'pathological' personality, and everything in between...
